cafc@cofc.note: Federal Circuit as entered by the CoFC plaintiff appealing a loss (plaintiff = appellant = self). Remand can only return to the CoFC.

deadline.note: 45 days after entry of judgment because the United States is a party to every CoFC appeal (Fed. Cir. R. 40, Federal Circuit Rules of Practice Dec. 1, 2025: 30 days, or 45 if the United States or its officer or agency is a party).

cafc@cofc-gov.note: Federal Circuit as entered by the United States appealing a CoFC plaintiff win. Perspective flipped: the government (appellant) is the opponent; payoffs are the plaintiff's (stake − appellant payoff, stake = $1M placeholder).

deadline.note: 45 days after entry of judgment because the United States is a party to every CoFC appeal (Fed. Cir. R. 40, Federal Circuit Rules of Practice Dec. 1, 2025: 30 days, or 45 if the United States or its officer or agency is a party).

cafc@ptab.note: Federal Circuit as entered from a PTAB final written decision (35 U.S.C. §§ 141, 319). Remand can only return to the PTAB.

cafc@itc.note: Federal Circuit as entered from an ITC § 337 final determination (19 U.S.C. § 1337(c)). Remand can only return to the Commission.

cafc@district-court.note: Federal Circuit as entered from a district-court patent judgment (28 U.S.C. § 1295(a)(1)): a civil action arising under the patent laws, or one with a compulsory patent counterclaim. Remand can only return to that district court.

links.label: Plaintiff appeals the judgment to the Federal Circuit
United States appeals the judgment for plaintiff
links.note: The government's appeal decision (Solicitor General authorization, 28 C.F.R. § 0.20(b)) is modeled as the opponent's choice; with no probability authored it is solved adversarially (worst case for the plaintiff). Author a probability here to use an appeal rate instead.

links.label: United States appeals the judgment entered for plaintiff
United States (or intervenor) appeals the sustained protest
Remand: further proceedings in the Court of Federal Claims
links.note: Re-entry point modeled as further merits proceedings (bench trial). A remand on a narrower issue re-enters later; override with scenario.mask/start when the mandate is specific.

links.label: Remand: further proceedings in the Court of Federal Claims
Appeal the final written decision to the Federal Circuit
links.note: Supersedes the PTAB pack's abstract Federal Circuit region when both packs are loaded; keeps its 0.92 appeal rate.

links.label: Remand: Board issues a new final written decision
Appeal the Commission's final determination to the Federal Circuit
links.note: Supersedes the ITC pack's abstract appeal edge when both packs are loaded.

links.label: Remand: Commission issues a new final determination
Proceed under FRAP in the regional circuit (detailed appellate track)
links.note: Non-patent civil appeals; the regional circuit is one of two routes out of `notice-of-appeal-filed` (see `frcp-appeal-to-cafc-district-court`). Which applies is a fact about the case (does it arise under the patent laws, or carry a compulsory patent counterclaim, 28 U.S.C. § 1295(a)(1)?), not a free choice between forums with concurrent jurisdiction — a matter scenario should `remove_edges` whichever of the two does not apply, the same way a `cafc@<origin>` instance keeps only the one true origin edge.

links.label: Proceed to the Federal Circuit (district-court patent judgment)
links.note: The Federal Circuit has exclusive jurisdiction over an appeal from a final district-court judgment in a civil action arising under an Act of Congress relating to patents (or plant variety protection), or in which a party asserted a compulsory patent counterclaim -- including a final judgment under 28 U.S.C. § 1292(c)(1)-(2). Coexists with `frcp-appeal-to-regional-circuit` as the other route out of `notice-of-appeal-filed`; a matter scenario selects the applicable one with `scenario.remove_edges` (see that link's note). Routes into the `cafc@district-court` instance, which mirrors `cafc@ptab`/`cafc@itc`/`cafc@cofc`: it keeps only `origin-to-district-court` and remands only back to the district court.
